To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inverse problem for potential flow around axisymmetric bodies can be solved by using the method of images.

(1) the solution to the inverse potential-flow problem of finding the singularities that produce a prescribed velocity distribution on an axisymmetric body can be expressed as the superposition of a linearly distributed axial singularity and a linearly distributed azimuthal singularity and that (2) the solution to this problem can be obtained in closed form.

(i) The solution for potential flow about an axisymmetric body with a prescribed pressure distribution on its surface can be obtained by superposing two potential flows: one due to the pressure distribution and the other due to a distribution of line singularities along the body axis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general theory for the flow about arbitrary three-dimensional bodies.
developing a numerical method for computing potential flow about axisymmetric bodies.
the application of the method of singularities to potential flow problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for the particular airfoil-type axisym-metric body of fineness = 2.9, the solution obtained by the present method of linearly varying singularities and the solution obtained from the exact equation for \I/Ij are the same.
the linear variation of axial singularities is not a good approximation to the exact solution, but it is a good approximation to a solution obtained by linear variation of axial sources.
the linearly distributed axial singularity model is a very good approximation of the actual flow field, but not a perfect one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linear variation in the axial singularities is a good approximation to the exact solution for the flow field around axisymmetric bodies.
the exact solution is very close to the linearly varying singularities solution.
the method of linearly varying singularities is a viable alternative to the use of conformal mapping for solving the direct and inverse axisymmetric flow problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solution of the potential flow problem is not sensitive to the distribution of axial singularities.
the inverse problem can be solved with the use of a single singularity.
the inverse problem can be solved with the same accuracy as the direct problem by using linearly varying axial sources.
